correctness.rationale: For triangular graph J(n,2), n>=5, Lipschitz-dual polar Q is defined on the canonical N=binom(n,2) vertex-coordinate zero-sum space, so primal inradius is the reciprocal of maximal centered Euclidean norm over 1-Lipschitz potentials. The oriented incidence inequality matrix is totally unimodular; strict convexity reduces maximizers to integral vertices, and diameter 2 reduces heights to {0,1,2}. Zero-height and two-height edges, viewed as edges of K_n, must have disjoint endpoint sets. The two-variable centered variance V(a,b)=a+b-(a-b)^2/N is dominated by maximal clique-edge counts in endpoint sets; the t>=n/4 derivative comparison and t<n/4 quadratic estimate force the balanced partition |S|=floor/ceil(n/2). This yields exact r_n=[(n-2)/n floor(n^2/4)]^-1/2, T_n balanced facet contacts and graph spread exactly 2(n-2)floor(n^2/4)/(n^2(n-1)). Centered indicator differences span the n-1 dimensional additive-edge subspace, leaving inball-center dimension N-n by strict slack at all other normals. Independent exhaustive standard Python enumeration of all 1133 normalized 3-level Lipschitz assignments for n=5 gave max N*norm²=36, 20 contacts; this is finite corroboration, with all-n proof by inequalities and linear rank.
